correctness.rationale: For every h>0, signs at prism vertices are s_j +/- t with sum s_j=0. An exhaustive k=0,1,2,3 vertical-edge classification proves N=4,5,4,3 respectively away from null boundaries. N=3 is the solid angle of a regular hexagonal cone; six determinant-formula spherical triangles yield T(h). Each of nine edges crosses with probability its endpoint angle/pi; summing gives L(h). Normalization and the expectation then give P4 and P5. The standalone nine-edge counter agrees with the analytic law at five heights over 900,000 uniform normals; finite tests are corroborative only.

value.rationale: The complete probability law for central sections of the simplest non-centrally-symmetric right prism is a natural geometric-probability benchmark. The support proof and regular-hexagonal solid-angle evaluation complement the known expected edge-crossing identity and produce the entire height-dependent distribution, including degenerate thin and tall limits. This is a motivated complete classification rather than an isolated arbitrary parameter slice.
